title: Find the first bad build
description:
A bug appeared somewhere in a list of builds numbered `0` to `count - 1`. Build 0 is known to be good and the last build is known to be bad; once a build is bad, every later build is bad too.

Write `firstBad(count, isBad)`, which returns the number of the first bad build. `isBad(n)` tests build `n`, and testing is slow, so the function must use as few tests as possible: a binary search, like `git bisect`. The tests count your calls.

You may assume `count >= 2`, `isBad(0)` is false and `isBad(count - 1)` is true; do not test those two.

```
count 10, builds 0..5 good, 6..9 bad  ->  6
```
hints: Keep two numbers: the latest build known to be good and the earliest known to be bad. Start with 0 and `count - 1`.
Test the build halfway between them. If it is bad, it becomes the new "earliest bad"; otherwise the new "latest good". Stop when they are next to each other: the bad one is the answer.
